acceptance: Only the owner can invite an accountant; second step required; no 'remember this device'; access ends on a date (sign-in refused after it, sessions revoked by the nightly sweep).

The accountant sees only Books, Taxes, Compliance, CPA Decisions, money reports and records Chris shares; every other route and function is refused (inventory tests: every requireRole/assertActiveTeamActor call enumerated, ACCOUNTANT only in the allowlist; a sample of 30 domain functions outside the list refused).
Allowed changes (adjustments, mappings, closes, reviewed marks, professional answers) are audited under the accountant's name and listed for Chris in the Books home feed and a Today card.
Never the vault, full tax ids, customer contact details, payments, refunds, sends or settings (tests).
Remove, reset sign-in, change end date and 'replace with a new accountant' work; history kept.
ci green at the exact head; every review comment read.
invariants: ACCOUNTANT is deny-by-default: it is added to no role list except the ones named in the spec's allowlist (section 2), and missing role data still denies. The allowlist test is the contract — if a function is not listed in the PR body, ACCOUNTANT must not reach it.

The accountant never reaches the vault (no unlock path exists for the role), never sees a full tax id (filing-account numbers stay masked), never sees customer contact details beyond names on bills, and has no send/charge/refund/payment/settings/team action anywhere.
Access end is enforced twice: at session validation (after accessEndsOn the person is refused with the spec's plain message) and by a nightly sweep that revokes the sessions of ended accountants.
Every accountant change is written by the existing domain functions and audited with the accountant's own user id; the owner's feed reads those audit rows — no shadow bookkeeping.

A business record is visible to the accountant only when the owner has marked it 'Share with my accountant' (new flag, default off); files follow the record, and an accountant upload lands on a shared record only, stamped 'Prepared by accountant'.

Second step for ACCOUNTANT follows the same owner setting mechanism as OWNER/ADMIN (twoFactorRequiredRoles), with ACCOUNTANT in the recommended default set; the two-factor page never offers an accountant a remembered device, and the trusted-device writer refuses the role as a backstop.
next: Build in sequence order; PR with the allowlist function list in the body; CI + Codex; merge; Lane 4's TAXBEN-2 unblocks.
outcome: The owner can invite his accountant (a CPA or tax professional) to their own sign-in: a new ACCOUNTANT level that requires a second step at every sign-in, is never offered 'remember this device', and ends on a date the owner sets. The accountant sees only Books, Taxes, Compliance, the money reports, the Decisions questions addressed to a CPA, and the business records the owner marks 'Share with my accountant' — everything else is refused at the screen layer and again inside each domain function. The changes the spec allows (adjusting entries, mappings, bank matches, fixed-asset fields, month closes, reviewed marks, professional answers, edits to prepared tax figures, uploads to shared records) are audited under the accountant's name, and the owner gets a 'Changes by your accountant' feed on Books home plus a Today card when there is something new. The owner can remove the accountant, reset their sign-in, change the end date, or replace them with a new accountant; history is kept.
